records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Felix,

Thanks for trying Wrenfield. A quick tip: projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them -- so the first few minutes are usually spent creating one project and adding a few tasks to it.

Let us know how it goes.

Thanks,
Chidi Haddad

decisions.rationale: 6 days in, no project, no invite, no key milestone, and zero replies to two outreach emails ([email:8b1a4c98], [email:e6d6f07e]) or tickets. Silent, fully unengaged accounts rarely self-activate in the remaining 8 days; Team plan purchase gives some upside.

draft.subject: A hand with your first Wrenfield project
draft.body:
Hi Felix,

I haven't heard back, so I wanted to check in once more rather than leave you guessing. In Wrenfield, projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, and the in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project. If it's useful, teammates can also be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Would a short call this week help? I can walk through setting up your first project with you and answer anything about how your team works today.

Best,
Chidi
